KAT26020 · PMAX and Google programmatic · MOF/BOF · Holiday Disaster

Holiday Disaster

The holiday mishap fills the frame. Everything sits on one centered axis: the headline across the top as two big solid label strips, setup in White and the punchline in Pink, then the photo melting into Dark Blue at the bottom, where the pink CTA, the logo and the disclaimer stack centered under it. V1 kitchen, V2 living room, same layout per size so only the imagery and copy change.

  • 16 frames
  • 2 iterations
  • 8 sizes each
  • V1/V2 static
V1 · Kitchen The turkey's fine. The oven isn't.

CTA: Shop Appliances. Lease to Own.

V2 · Living room Cyber deals are here. Let Katapult help.

CTA: Lease new furniture before family arrives

For review. All 16 built. Open questions for the account lead are in the production notes: the disclaimer (from the Figma frames, not the brief) and its sizes.

Images are the two the client likes, not regenerated. Only lightened, as the brief asks: midtones and shadows lifted, a touch of contrast put back so the flat Eggleston look doesn't go hazy, and the orange cast trimmed so the whites read white. Nothing in the pictures was changed.

Framing (round 2, full-bleed): the photo fills the whole frame, cropped around the mishap so the turkey or the tree always lands mid-frame, clear of the type. The headline never sits loose on the picture: each line is a solid strip (White strip with Dark Blue type, then Dark Blue strip with Pink type), so it reads on any part of the photo. The photo fades into solid Dark Blue at the bottom, where the CTA, disclaimer and logo sit; the logo is never on the photo. On 728x90 and 320x50 the photo takes the right end of the banner and fades into the Dark Blue that carries logo, headline and CTA. Round 1 (photo in a circle on Dark Blue) was replaced in internal review. Round 3: headline, CTA, logo and disclaimer centered on the frame, and the headline pushed to the full safe width, since nothing else competes with it. The leaderboards keep their one-row order (logo, headline, CTA, photo).

Type: Aktiv Grotesk Bold, tight leading. First sentence on White, second in Pink: the color break is the punchline. Each size uses the largest headline that fits both versions, so V1 and V2 match in size and position.

Copy is the client's, verbatim, only broken into lines. V2's CTA has no period, as in the brief. CTA is the brand pink pill with white text.

Disclaimer: not in the brief's copy, but the account lead placed one in the Figma 4x5 frames ("Lease-purchase service. Total cost exceeds cash price. Approval required. Not available in MN, NJ, WI, WY. See katapult.com."). Carried verbatim on the three PMAX sizes. Left off programmatic, where there's no legible room and earlier Katapult jobs ran without it. To confirm with the account lead.

Safe zones: 5% inset on PMAX, 4 to 12px on programmatic. Checked by script on every frame: logo, copy and CTA inside the safe zone, nothing overlapping, nothing covering the mishap, and logo, CTA and disclaimer on the solid part of the fade.

KAT26022 · PMAX and Google programmatic · TOF · Trusted

Trusted

Two directions, each built in all 8 sizes. Same copy, same Dark Blue ground, same logo corner and the same single trust signal: a Trustpilot badge with stars and wordmark only, no quote, no invented number. The account lead picks one to deliver.

  • 16 frames
  • 2 options
  • 8 sizes each
  • V1 static
Option A Centered badge

All graphic. Copy centered at the top, a large circle rising from the bottom, the badge in the middle of a halo of blurred review cards. Figma 383:14304. 8 sizes.

Option B Photo and seam badge

A shopper photo across the top half, copy stacked left on the Dark Blue panel below, the badge card bridging the seam on the right. Figma 387:14518. 8 sizes, photo shown as a placeholder until the real one is in.

Headline
Don't take our word for it.
Subhead
Real people, real reviews. There's a reason why thousands rate Katapult 5 stars.
CTA
See Why Shoppers Love Katapult.

Next: the account lead picks A or B for final delivery. Still pending from the client: the real shopper photo for B, and real Trustpilot quotes, TrustScore and badge file if they are meant to appear.

Pass history, 1 to 7

Seventh pass: 8 sizes x 2 options, 16 frames. Scope grew from the 1200x1200 approval pair to every size in both directions. The two 1200x1200 frames keep the Figma numbers from pass 6 exactly (both nodes above). The other 7 sizes of each option carry the same language: A keeps copy centered at the top, the #282B60 circle rising behind the badge and the halo of blurred star-only cards, logo bottom-right; B keeps the photo band, the badge card bridging the photo's edge on the right, copy stacked left on the Dark Blue panel and the logo bottom-right on the panel, never on the photo. On 1200x628 B the photo becomes a left band and the badge bridges its right edge at the top. On 728x90 and 320x50 both options collapse to one row: logo, copy, trust element, CTA. In B there the photo shrinks to a small tab the badge hangs from.

Photo placeholder in Option B, on purpose. The shopper photo synced from Figma in pass 6 is replaced in every B frame, the 1200x1200 included, by this brand's own placeholder (Light Blue fill, dashed Dark Blue outline, "Photo placeholder", same as the Q4 organic kit). The real photo goes in by another route. Until then B in the hub looks different from the Figma frame, which is expected.

Type floors. Nothing under the higher of KAT26019 and KAT26021 at each size (logo, headline, subhead, CTA): 1200x628 200/58/26/28, 960x1200 220/76/34/34, 300x600 100/29/15/17, 160x600 88/24/12/13, 300x250 76/20.5/10/12, 728x90 96/25/-/13, 320x50 46/14/-/8. Built at: 1200x628 A 200/72/28/28, B 200/64/28/28; 960x1200 A 220/109.67/42.18/42.18 (the 1200 numbers fit 864px), B 220/92/36/34; 300x600 A 100/41/17/17, B 100/40/17/17; 160x600 A 88/32/14/13, B 88/30/13/13; 300x250 A 76/22/10.5/12, B 76/21/10/12; 728x90 both 96/25/11/13; 320x50 both 46/14/6/8.

Open question: the subhead at 728x90 and 320x50. Both precedent jobs drop the subhead at these two sizes; this brief puts it on every size, so it stays (11px and 6px). At 320x50 it isn't really readable. Dropping it there needs the account lead's OK.

Verified by rendering, not by eye: headless Chrome with the real Aktiv Grotesk loaded, Actual size on, getBoundingClientRect read back frame-relative for every element of all 16 frames. Every frame: headline, subhead, CTA, logo and badge (cream plate included) inside the safe zone; no overlap between them, checked line by line on the text; no blurred card over copy, CTA or logo; the circle behind no text line; the photo under no copy and never under the logo; CTA text inside its pill; badge wordmark and stars inside the card; copy joined back from the line breaks equals the brief word for word. Then every frame screenshotted and looked at.

Sixth pass: synced from Figma. The V1 static now mirrors the frame the account lead adjusted in Figma (Progressive Global - LAB, page "kat", node 383:14304): headline, subhead and CTA centered on the frame instead of stacked left, headline in Medium at 110px, subhead 42px in two lines, CTA pill 779x108, a large #282B60 circle rising from the bottom behind the badge, badge 499x230 centered at 600,852, and the five blurred review cards at Figma's own sizes, angles and blur. Logo stays 230px in the bottom-right corner. Copy unchanged. The notes below are the history of passes 1 to 5.

Status at passes 1 to 6: 1200x1200 only, built for approval before the other 7 sizes.

Rebuilt again, direction changed. The first pass (a flat 2x3 grid with a soft drop shadow) was rejected for having no art direction. The second pass (a STACK of twelve review cards) is dropped here, in full, not shrunk or thinned out: we have no real Trustpilot quotes, we can't invent them, and a wall of twelve cards repeating the same bracketed placeholder line reads as exactly what it is, fake reviews. That's a false-advertising risk, not a placeholder detail, so the device itself is gone.

This version leads with a photo instead. Same skeleton as two approved Q4 organic slides (p04-s2 "The Refrigerator Stops Working" and p04-s3 "The Car Needs New Tires," BLOCK mechanic, see art-direction-v2.md): a full-bleed photo across the top ~58% of the frame, a Dark Blue panel below carrying the headline and subhead exactly as written, and one small floating white card bridging the seam. The photo is a labeled placeholder (role="img", same convention as the organic build's kp-ph slots), not a fabricated image, pending a real shopper photo. The subhead's own line, "Real people, real reviews," is the case for leading with a real photo instead of an all-graphic composition.

The one trust element left is a single badge, not a wall: five Trustpilot-green stars and the word "Trustpilot," no quote, no invented TrustScore or review count. It lives only in the floating seam card.

Logo moved off the photo on purpose. Katapult's artwork never sits on top of a photo, so it's placed near the headline on the Dark Blue panel instead of the top corner it held over the old card wall.

Color is Dark Blue ground below the photo, matching the rest of the Banners channel, so the CTA stays the brand's pink pill with white text.

Safe zones: 5% inset on PMAX for copy, logo, badge and CTA. The photo itself bleeds flush to all three top edges, same as a real photo would.

Third pass: typography, not structure. Pass 2 kept this skeleton but shipped every type element smaller than this brand's own approved precedent on the same 1200x1200 Dark-Blue-ground family (KAT26019: logo 230, headline 84, subhead 36, cta 36/26/54; KAT26021: logo 240, cta 34/24/52). The cause was allocation, not the numbers themselves: the photo band was eating 700 of 1200px, leaving too little room below it. Fixed by dropping the photo to 560px (47% of the frame) and re-spacing the panel, landing on logo 230px, headline 84px, subhead 36px, CTA 36px with 26px/54px padding, matching or exceeding both precedents. Checked by rendering the actual markup with the real Aktiv Grotesk font loaded and reading back getComputedStyle font sizes and getBoundingClientRect boxes, not by eye: every element sits inside the 60px safe inset with no overlap (CTA's lowest point lands at y=1111, the safe edge is at 1140).

Fourth pass: two targeted changes from the account lead, off a reference ad ("CodeWizardsHQ," a different brand, only its structure carried over, never its copy or numbers).

1. CTA detached from the column, moved to the bottom-right corner. It no longer sits left-aligned under the subhead; it's anchored right:60px;bottom:60px, inside the same 60px safe inset as everything else. Freeing its old slot opened room in the stacked logo/headline/subhead column, used to re-space that column (not to shrink it) once the badge change below pushed on the same space. Logo stays 230px wide, headline stays 84px, subhead stays 36px, all at the approved KAT26019 floor, never under it.

2. The Trustpilot badge is now a large, centered card instead of a small off-right chip. Same general seam position as before (straddling the photo/panel boundary), just bigger and centered on the frame's horizontal middle. Stars + "Trustpilot" wordmark only, sized up (stars 62px, wordmark 42px), still no numeric TrustScore or review count: we don't have Katapult's real number and won't invent one. Depth on the badge itself stays this brand's flat offset plate (20px 20px 0 #D4A574), not a blurred shadow.

Blurred decorative texture added around the badge, over the photo only. Five small white review-card shapes (rounded rect + a mini star row, no quote text) sit scattered behind/around the big badge, each with a CSS filter:blur(7px). This is the account lead's own fix for the real problem with this job: we have no approved real Trustpilot quotes to show (see the blocking item above), so anything legible in that space would be a fabricated testimonial. Blurring removes the "legible claim" problem at the root: zoomed crops confirm the star rows dissolve into unreadable color smudges, not stylized-but-readable text. This is a different technique from this brand's flat-plate card-depth rule above: blur is for this decorative atmosphere texture only, never for simulating real UI elevation.

Verified by rendering and measuring, not eyeballing (real Aktiv Grotesk, getBoundingClientRect read back frame-relative, with the preview's 0.4 display scale normalized to 1:1 first). Final numbers on the 1200x1200: badge 376,449 to 824,671 (447x222), centered on the frame's x midpoint and the same y=560 seam as the old chip. Five deco cards, all within the photo band (lowest bottom edge y=379), none overlapping the badge or each other. Logo 230px at top=702 (31px clear of the badge's new bottom edge). Headline 84px at top=767. Subhead 36px at top=941, three lines ending at y=1070. CTA right=1140/bottom=1140 (touching the safe edge exactly, not past it), top=1047/left=469: checked line-by-line against the subhead's own last line (which ends at x=399), so the CTA and subhead text never actually touch despite their bounding boxes appearing to overlap on paper.

Fifth pass: two corrections from the account lead, one a straight mistake, one a real layout change. First, pass 4's own instruction was "leave the Katapult button in the corner," meaning the logo, not the CTA; pass 4 moved the CTA there instead. Fixed by swapping which element uses that anchoring: the right:60px;bottom:60px corner slot now holds the logo (still 230px wide, the approved floor, no reason to grow it), and the CTA is back in the stacked column, left-aligned at x=60 below the subhead, where it sat before pass 4 pulled it out. Second, the full-bleed photo is gone entirely this pass: the account lead asked to drop the imagery, enlarge the blurred cards, and pull them in tighter around the central Trustpilot modal, so the frame is back to a bare #131540 Dark Blue canvas with no seam. The badge itself (447x222, stars 62px, wordmark 42px, flat offset plate, no numeric score) is untouched, just recentered. The deco cards grew (padding 16/24 to 34/48, star font 15 to 30, each card now roughly 240-255px wide by 110-135px tall depending on its rotation) and moved from loosely scattered across the photo band to five positions clustered tight around the badge at its corners and bottom-center, several of them overlapping the badge's own edge on purpose (the badge sits above them at z-index 2) so the group reads as a pile the badge sits inside, not background confetti. Still a star row only, no quote, still filter:blur(), never the flat-plate technique.

Full vertical layout recomputed now that the photo's 560px is out of play and the full 1200px of frame height is available. Headline 92px (above the 84px floor) at top=70, box 60,70 to 679.6,242.9. Subhead 40px (above the 36px floor) at top=272, box 60,272 to 636.9,416, three lines. CTA 40px/28px/58px (above the 36px floor) at top=456, box 60,456 to 781.3,558. Badge centered at 600,848, box 376.4,738 to 823.6,958. Logo 230px (at the floor) anchored to the corner, box 910,1088.8 to 1140,1140. Five deco cards: top-left 210.3,650.8 to 463.7,785.2; top-right 737.9,652.7 to 990.1,783.3; bottom-left 222.1,936.7 to 471.9,1059.3; bottom-right 728.4,934.7 to 979.6,1061.3; bottom-center 477.1,992.8 to 722.9,1103.2. Checked programmatically, not by eye: no pairwise overlap among logo/headline/subhead/cta; no overlap between the badge or any deco card and logo/headline/subhead/cta (closest approach is the bottom-right deco card to the logo, 27.5px clear vertically); logo/headline/subhead/cta and the badge+cluster's own bounding region (210.3,650.8 to 990.1,1103.2) all sit fully inside the 60px safe inset. A zoomed crop of a deco card at 3x confirms the bigger star row still dissolves into soft color blobs under the blur, not legible stars or text.

Copy is the client's, placed exactly as written. The headline is only broken into lines, with each sentence starting on its own line. Subhead on the PMAX sizes and 300x600; 160x600, 300x250, 728x90 and 320x50 carry headline and CTA only, the Katapult banner default. No disclaimer, because the brief's copy has none.

Client note: lean into the knolling shot, not things floating on white. Every product is now shot from straight above and laid flat on a matte, very light salmon ground, at right angles, with even gutters and one key light, so the frame reads as a real flat-lay. Same copy, logo, type and CTA sizes as the approved round 2, all 8 sizes, V1 static and V2 animated storyboards. PMAX shown at 40%, programmatic at 100%.

V1 · Static

V2 · Animated storyboards

Three scenes per size. S01 logo and products, S02 the products trade places and the headline lands, S03 is the end frame and matches V1. Copy is hidden, never moved, so nothing jumps between scenes.

Production notes

Images: eight products generated with AI as top-down shots on white (sofa, TV, tire, refrigerator, bed, laptop, washing machine, game console), then silhouetted with their own contact shadow kept, so they sit on the ground instead of floating. No brand, logo or text on any product.

Arrangement: rows of products, each row sharing one height and running edge to edge across its area. The subhead's three nouns (couch, TV, tire) lead wherever there's room: 8 products on PMAX and 300x600, 4 on 160x600 and 300x250, 3 on 728x90, the sofa alone on 320x50.

Ground: very light salmon #F6E6DE, with a fine paper grain and a soft lift at top left from the same key light the shadows fall away from.
